description: Each rating's share is its number of distinct rented films as a fraction of the total distinct rented films summed over ratings.

c.request: Looking at what has actually been rented (each rental traced through its inventory copy to the film, skipping any that don't link up), what share of the rented films does each film `rating` account for, out of the total across all ratings? For the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, give one row with: their combined number of rented films, their average share, and how far on average their share sits above that average share. No rounding. Each rating's share is its number of distinct rented films as a fraction of the total distinct rented films summed over ratings.
c.sql:
WITH rented_films AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT f.film_id, f.rating
  FROM rental r
  JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
),
rating_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    rating,
    COUNT(*) as film_count,
    COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rented_films) as share
  FROM rented_films
  GROUP BY rating
),
avg_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_value FROM rating_shares
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT 
    film_count,
    share
  FROM rating_shares
  CROSS JOIN avg_share
  WHERE share > avg_share.avg_value
)
SELECT
  SUM(film_count) as combined_rented_films,
  AVG(share) as average_share,
  AVG(share - (SELECT avg_value FROM avg_share)) as avg_above_average
FROM above_average

a.request: Link each rental to its inventory copy and that copy's film, dropping rentals with no matching copy or film. For each film `rating`, count the distinct films that were rented, so each film counts once however often it was rented. Compute each rating's share as its count divided by the total of these counts across all ratings. Keep only the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, with each rating weighted equally. Return a single row with: the total count of those ratings, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. Do not round anything.
a.sql: WITH rental_film_link AS (SELECT r.rental_id, i.inventory_id, i.film_id, f.rating FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id), rating_film_counts AS (SELECT rating, COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) AS film_count FROM rental_film_link GROUP BY rating), total_films AS (SELECT SUM(film_count) AS total_count FROM rating_film_counts), rating_shares AS (SELECT rating, film_count, film_count / (SELECT total_count FROM total_films) AS share FROM rating_film_counts), average_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM rating_shares), filtered_ratings AS (SELECT rs.rating, rs.film_count, rs.share, (SELECT avg_share FROM average_share) AS avg_share FROM rating_shares rs WHERE rs.share > (SELECT avg_share FROM average_share)) SELECT SUM(film_count) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS average_excess FROM filtered_ratings

d.request: For each of the five film ratings, calculate the share as the count of distinct films with that rating that were rented (connected via rental → inventory → film) divided by the total count of distinct rented films across all ratings; identify ratings where this share exceeds the mean share across all five ratings; and for those above-average ratings, output a single row with their combined distinct rented film count, the mean of their individual shares, and the mean amount their individual shares exceed the overall mean share.
d.sql: WITH rented_films AS (SELECT DISTINCT f.film_id, f.rating FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id), rating_counts AS (SELECT rating, COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) as rented_count FROM rented_films GROUP BY rating), total_rented AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) as total_rented_films FROM rented_films), shares AS (SELECT rc.rating, rc.rented_count, CAST(rc.rented_count AS DECIMAL(10,4)) / CAST(tr.total_rented_films AS DECIMAL(10,4)) as share FROM rating_counts rc CROSS JOIN total_rented tr), mean_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share FROM shares), above_average AS (SELECT s.rating, s.rented_count, s.share, s.share - ms.avg_share as excess FROM shares s CROSS JOIN mean_share ms WHERE s.share > ms.avg_share) SELECT SUM(rented_count) as combined_rented_count, AVG(share) as mean_share, AVG(excess) as mean_excess FROM above_average

b.request: For each film rating, calculate its share as the count of distinct films with that rating in at least one rental divided by the total count of distinct films across all ratings in at least one rental; for ratings whose share exceeds the average share across all ratings, return one row with the sum of their distinct rented film counts, the mean of their shares, and the mean amount by which their individual shares exceed the overall average share.
b.sql:
WITH rented_films_by_rating AS (
  SELECT 
    f.rating,
    COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) as distinct_films
  FROM film f
  JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  JOIN rental r ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
total_rented_films AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) as total_films
  FROM film f
  JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  JOIN rental r ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
),
ratings_with_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    rf.rating,
    rf.distinct_films,
    rf.distinct_films / tr.total_films as share
  FROM rented_films_by_rating rf
  CROSS JOIN total_rented_films tr
),
average_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share
  FROM ratings_with_shares
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT 
    rws.rating,
    rws.distinct_films,
    rws.share,
    rws.share - avg.avg_share as excess
  FROM ratings_with_shares rws
  CROSS JOIN average_share avg
  WHERE rws.share > avg.avg_share
)
SELECT 
  SUM(distinct_films) as sum_distinct_films,
  AVG(share) as mean_share,
  AVG(excess) as mean_excess
FROM above_average
